# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 13: One Company Cut Its AI Chat Costs 75%


### Hex took nearly 75% off the cost of each AI chat, Anthropic’s IPO is set to price Wednesday, the FT says Jensen Huang has discussed a return, and Korea’s GPU plan still stands.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 17, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/5TohYKDQkltfS8lzH22KFq) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/tMFzums5ji8) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week: Anthropic’s IPO is set to price on Wednesday. At the top of its range it would raise $62.5 billion, more than twice what Saudi Aramco’s IPO raised in 2019. The Financial Times reports that Jensen Huang has discussed a return as Nvidia’s CEO, and the Treasury Secretary says Nvidia should hire from outside. South Korea says Nvidia still plans up to 260,000 GPUs for the country. And in the Department of Token Efficiency, Hex took nearly 75% off the cost of each chat. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## The tokens


The world runs about


**470 trillion tokens a day** , per


[tokensperday.com](https://tokensperday.com/) as of 16 November. That’s about


**57,000 for every person on Earth** , and the count is up a trillion since yesterday on the site’s own clock. Fifty-seven thousand each. Mine are mostly “make it shorter.”


Over on OpenRouter, usage of Tencent’s


**Hy4** grew


**42% in a week** (


[OpenRouter rankings](https://openrouter.ai/rankings) ). That’s just one platform. Somebody at Tencent gets a bonus. Somebody else gets the bill.


---


## The landlord’s rate card


*“Rent’s down, darling. My accountant needs a lie-down.”*


On the Ornn Compute Price Index, which tracks actual rentals, as of the 15 November settle:


-


**NVIDIA H100** settled at


**$3.06 an hour** , down about


**4%** since yesterday but still up about


**4%** over the month (


[Ornn H100](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/H100%20SXM/index-history) ). A one-day discount on a one-month markup. The landlord still comes out ahead.


-


**B200** settled at


**$9.66 an hour** , unchanged since yesterday and up about


**22%** over the month (


[Ornn B200](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/B200/index-history) ). Renters pay more for the same chip.


---


## Chips, power and the work


**Chips.** Epoch counts about


**34 million AI chips** , measured in Nvidia H100s. That’s still its latest count, from 21 October (


[Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-sales) ). Epoch tracks


**96 data centres** and estimates they hold about


**44%** of those chips (


[Epoch AI data centres](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers) ). Somewhere out there, a chip is idle. And billing you.


**Power.** The data centres behind these chips draw about


**30 gigawatts** , our estimate from Epoch’s tracker. Last year, AI data centres used about


**half a percent of the world’s electricity** , and about


**a tenth of a percent** of all the energy we use. Both are our estimates, built from International Energy Agency figures (


[Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/how-much-energy-do-data-centers-and-artificial-intelligence-use) ).


**The work.** Our name for it this week is


**SI: Stock-listed Intelligence** . Now with a quiet period.


On our bet, SI does about


**11.7% of the hours we work** , about


**41 minutes a day** for everyone who still has a Monday. Workers themselves say AI saves them about


**2% of their hours** , per the St. Louis Fed’s July survey (


[FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RPSGENAITSALL) ). That works out to about seven minutes a day, our estimate. SI would like a word with HR.


Economist James Bessen checked all


**271 jobs** in the 1950 US census. By 2010, automation had wiped out just one of them:


**elevator operator** (


[Bessen, NBER](https://conference.nber.org/confer/2016/SI2016/PRIT/Bessen.pdf) ). The only job that went down was the one that took you up.


These numbers are a work in progress. Got better data? Step boldly into our DMs.


---


## The news: Nvidia


The Financial Times reports that


**Jensen Huang has discussed a return** as Nvidia’s CEO with close confidants. CNBC carried the report on Sunday night (


[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/nvidia-jensen-huang-return-tech.html) ).


**Colette Kress** remains interim CEO.


The petition to bring Huang back now says it has


**more than 160,000 signatures** . The petition doesn’t verify its signers’ affiliations.


Treasury Secretary


**Scott Bessent** told Fox News on Sunday that Nvidia should hire an outside chief executive (


[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/bessent-nvidia-ceo-lutnick-megaspeed.html) ).


Nvidia reports earnings on


**Tuesday, 17 November** . Expect the word “interim” to get a workout on that call.


*Per-dollar verdict: your next GPU quote comes with a succession plan.*


---


## Korea


South Korea’s science minister says Nvidia still plans


**up to 260,000 GPUs** for the country. Yonhap reported it on Friday, a day after the CEO change (


[Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261113008400320) ). The named partners are


**Samsung, SK Group, Hyundai Motor Group and Naver Cloud** .


Nvidia first put that number on the table a year ago (


[NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/south-korea-ai-infrastructure) ). So far, it’s a plan on paper. A commitment to deploy is a save-the-date. The wedding is TBD.


*Per-dollar verdict: “up to” is doing a lot of work. Ask any sale sign.*


---


## Anthropic’s IPO


Anthropic’s IPO is set to price on


**Wednesday** . Trading is due to start


**Thursday** , on the Nasdaq, under


**ANT** (


[Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/roadshow-launch) ;


[MSCI](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?format=html&lang=en&pub_key=4HJms64tFsA%3D) ).


The price range tops out at


**$78 a share** . At that price, Anthropic would raise about


**$62.5 billion** from its own shares. That’s more than twice what


**Saudi Aramco’s IPO** raised in 2019, about $29.4 billion (


[Aramco](https://www.aramco.com/-/media/images/investors/saudi-aramco-final-price-announcement-en.pdf) ).


The prospectus is long. Your AI will summarize it. For a fee.


*Per-dollar verdict: when your vendor has shareholders, your discount has competition.*


---


## The tier list


How many dollars of API usage you get per dollar of subscription, on our 16 November run of Adam Holter’s method with


[Real API Pricing](https://github.com/Fei2411/real-api-pricing) . And they’re off!


[Adam Holter @AdamHoltererer Subsidization varies across users and usage patterns Some users get a lot more subsidization than others, but all of them get a ton This could be because the API rates for different types of tokens, such as cached input and output, might be different than the usage rates 10:51 PM · Nov 7, 2026 · 11.9K Views 8 Replies · 2 Reposts · 104 Likes](https://x.com/AdamHoltererer/status/2119201175904149984)


-


**Claude Max** breaks first, at about


**$77** of API value per plan dollar.


-


**Claude Ultra** runs second at about


**$66** , and


**Claude Pro** is a neck behind in third at about


**$64** . A Claude trifecta. The track is considering a name change.


-


Into the turn: Claude Max on Haiku takes fourth, and Google’s biggest Ultra plan is fifth, on Flash. Claude Ultra on Haiku is sixth at about


**$47** , Claude Pro on Haiku seventh at about


**$46** , and X Ultra eighth at


**$43.70 or better** . The stewards are still reviewing that one.


-


Ninth and tenth:


**ChatGPT’s $200 and $100 Pro plans** , both in the high twenties. OpenAI is racing itself.


-


Trailing the field, last of 44:


**Google AI Pro on Gemini Argon** , at about


**$1.40** . Argon is still looking for the starting gate.


Google’s pricing page says the Flash model behind fifth place


**doubles in price on 1 January** (


[Gemini API pricing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing) ). Pay by the token, and you pay twice as much. Same horse. Twice the oats.


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Chainsaw fueled. Spreadsheets open.


**Cut one: Hex** , which makes a data agent (


[Hex](https://hex.tech/blog/crashing-the-cost-of-data-intelligence/) ).


-


Each chat with its agent cost


**$6.44** at its January peak. Now it’s


**$1.64** . That’s nearly


**75% cheaper** .


-


Hex got there with a cheaper model and a leaner agent. On Hex’s own test, OpenAI’s Luna trails Opus, and costs


**a tenth as much, or less** .


-


Hex also fixed expensive cache misses.


You know who lives in that chat log. Cheaper per chat? Wonderful. He’ll simply attend more chats. We might get rid of the goblin, but Jevons is here to stay.


**The fine print:** Hex’s own blog, measured from January’s peak. Token use grew almost a hundredfold in a year. No total bill.


**Cut two: Modem** swapped one database for another (


[Modem](https://modem.ai/blog/pgvector-to-turbopuffer) ).


-


It dropped


**pgvector** , an add-on for Postgres. Now it uses


**turbopuffer** , a search database.


-


Modem says its whole storage bill fell


**10%** , even after paying for turbopuffer.


-


On day one, processor load on its main database fell


**62%** . Postgres finally got a four-day week.


**The fine print:** Modem’s own blog, rounded figures, no dollar amounts. The savings are database costs.


**Cut three: alkemy** runs an AI research agent (


[alkemy](https://alkemyos.com/blog/llm-cost-optimization) ).


-


Nearly


**40%** of each prompt turned out to be tool instructions.


-


alkemy trimmed that and added caching, plus a few other fixes. In its tests, the average research brief now costs


**less than half** as much.


The agent spent 40% of its prompt reading its own manual. Relatable.


**The fine print:** alkemy’s own blog. Test workloads only. No dollar figures.
